The issue lies in the method `DiscreteDistribution.sample(int)`. This method creates an array `out` using `java.lang.reflect.Array.newInstance(singletons.get(0).getClass(), sampleSize)`. If the first element of `singletons` is of a subclass type `T1` and `sample()` method returns an object of type `T` but not of type `T1`, it can result in an exception.

In the failing test `testIssue942()`, the `List` is created with elements of type `Object` and `Double`, which may lead to the scenario described in the bug report.

To fix this issue, the method `sample(int)` in `DiscreteDistribution` needs to be modified to handle the case when the types of objects returned by `sample()` and the first element of `singletons` are not compatible.

Next, I will provide recommendations for where to fix this issue.
